mappings.note: degree read off the highest power of a univariate polynomial - the first clause of LO-1; nothing is evaluated or modelled
asks for the coefficient of a named term; no learning outcome under C-2.1 covers coefficients (LO-1 is degree only, LO-2 is polynomial-or-not), so the competency is cited rather than stretching LO-1
picks the degree-one expression out of four - LO-1's 'names a polynomial of degree one as linear' clause applied as a classification
constant term of a cubic; like item 2 there is no outcome for term identification, only for degree, so the competency is the honest ceiling
substitutes a value into a finished linear rule 5x-3, the 'uses it to predict' half of LO-2; it does not have to build the rule, which is what separates it from items 24 and 30
the tile rule 2n-1 is supplied and a far term (stage 15) is predicted - the textbook case of LO-2; the pattern is not tested for constant differences, so not LO-1
the graded answer is the classification 'linear polynomial' by degree, so LO-1; the match-cost wording is scenery, nothing is modelled or predicted, so not C-3.2-LO-3
identifies the slope of a linear relationship; the closest legal code, though LO-5 is worded 'from the graph' and this item supplies the equation - see the defect note for this chapter
the y-intercept half of LO-5, paired with item 8 which takes the slope half; again read from the equation, not a graph
distinguishes linear growth from decay and from non-linear forms among four candidate models - LO-3 is the only outcome that names growth and decay
writes a rule of the form ax+b (4x) for a quantity, which is LO-2's first clause; imperfect because LO-2 presumes a pattern of terms and this rule comes from a geometric definition
asks what the intercept must be for the line to pass through the origin - the 'predicts the effect of changing the intercept' clause of LO-6, not the read-off of LO-5
tests successive differences of a sequence for constancy, which is exactly LO-1; no rule is written, so not LO-2
evaluates a QUADRATIC at s=0; C-3.2-LO-2 is restricted to linear rules and C-2.1-LO-1 is degree only, so only the competency fits - poor fit, recorded as such
equal slopes with different intercepts give parallel lines - the first clause of LO-6 stated as a general fact
classification by degree again, this time degree zero; the same 'degree from the highest power' skill as item 3, not a polynomial-or-not test
assertion and reason together are LO-1 verbatim - degree one names a linear polynomial
the false reason is 'linear decay has positive slope', so the discriminating knowledge is the sign of the slope under decay (LO-3); reading slope -3 off y=-3x is the secondary step (LO-5)
interprets a as rate and b as fixed charge in a billing situation - LO-5's 'interprets each in the situation being modelled', which is what makes it different from the bare read-offs at items 8 and 9
the reason clause is the constant-difference test itself, which is LO-1; no far term is predicted, so not LO-2
degree of the polynomial is LO-1; the constant-term half has no outcome at all, so the competency carries it
constructs polynomials to order by degree - LO-1 run in reverse, which is still degree-from-highest-power knowledge
same finished rule as item 5 evaluated at a negative value; substitution into ax+b, not the building of it
builds 15n-5 from a worded fare situation with a fixed part and a per-unit part - modelling linear growth (LO-3); there is no table of terms, which is what LO-2 presumes
states both slope and intercept of a given line - LO-5 with both clauses, but again from the equation and with no situation to interpret them in
